claims.source: Previous genetic screens have identified MORPHEUS MOLECULE 1 (MOM1) (Amedeo et al., 2000; Won et al., 2012), and MICRORCHIDIA 1 and 6 (MORC1 and MORC6) (Moissiard et al., 2012; Lorković et al., 2012; Brabbs et al., 2013), as genes that are required for the silencing of methylated loci but that do not control the levels of DNA methylation (Amedeo et al., 2000; Won et al., 2012; Moissiard et al., 2012; Lorković et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to prior studies.

claims.claim: MICRORCHIDIA 1 and 6 (MORC1 and MORC6) are required for the silencing of methylated loci but do not control the levels of DNA methylation.
claims.source: Previous genetic screens have identified MORPHEUS MOLECULE 1 (MOM1) (Amedeo et al., 2000; Won et al., 2012), and MICRORCHIDIA 1 and 6 (MORC1 and MORC6) (Moissiard et al., 2012; Lorković et al., 2012; Brabbs et al., 2013), as genes that are required for the silencing of methylated loci but that do not control the levels of DNA methylation (Amedeo et al., 2000; Won et al., 2012; Moissiard et al., 2012; Lorković et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to prior studies.

claims.claim: Mutations in ARABIDOPSIS TRITHORAX-RELATED PROTEIN 5 and 6 (atxr5 and atxr6) release gene silencing without significantly altering the pattern of DNA methylation.
claims.source: In addition, mutations in ARABIDOPSIS TRITHORAX-RELATED PROTEIN 5 and 6 (atxr5 and atxr6) (Jacob et al., 2009) were also found to release gene silencing without significantly altering the pattern of DNA methylation.
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation to a prior study.

claims.claim: SU(VAR)3–9 HOMOLOG 1 (SUVH1) acts downstream of DNA methylation to enable the transcription of methylated loci.
claims.source: On the other hand, only one factor, SU(VAR)3–9 HOMOLOG 1 (SUVH1) (Li et al., 2016), has been identified to act downstream of DNA methylation to enable the transcription of methylated loci.
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation to a prior study.

claims.claim: The YJ and LUCH reporters differ in their basal levels of LUC expression despite harboring nearly identical transgenes.
claims.source: Here we compared the expression patterns and epigenetic features of the two LUC reporters, which differ in their basal levels of LUC expression despite harboring nearly identical transgenes that contain LUC genes driven by dual cauliflower mosaic virus 35S promoters (d35S) (Figure 1—source data 1, Figure 1—figure supplements 1A,B).
claims.evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study's characterization of the reporters.

claims.claim: At the d35S promoters, the YJ and LUCH transgenes had similar patterns of 24-nt siRNAs and similar levels of DNA methylation in all sequence contexts.
claims.source: At the d35S promoters, the two transgenes had similar patterns of 24-nt siRNAs and similar levels of DNA methylation in all sequence contexts (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C,D).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a finding from sequencing data shown in the referenced figure.

claims.claim: In LUCH, DNA methylation extended beyond the d35S promoters into the LUC and NPTII coding regions.
claims.source: However, in LUCH, DNA methylation extended beyond the d35S promoters into the LUC and NPTII coding regions (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C,D).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a finding from sequencing data shown in the referenced figure.

claims.claim: Analysis of the MethylC-seq data supports the conclusion that the YJ and LUCH reporters represent single and multi-copy insertions into a single genomic locus, respectively.
claims.source: Although both reporters segregate as single-copy insertions, analysis of the MethylC-seq data supports the conclusion that the YJ and LUCH reporters represent single and multi-copy insertions into a single genomic locus, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from analysis of MethylC-seq data shown in the referenced figure.

claims.claim: Both YJ and LUCH reporters contain genes that harbor high levels of promoter methylation but are not fully silenced.
claims.source: Despite these differences, both reporters share a common feature that distinguishes them from most endogenous methylated loci: they contain genes that harbor high levels of promoter methylation but are not fully silenced.
claims.evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study's characterization of the reporters.

claims.claim: Two mutants with reduced luciferase luminescence were identified from independent genetic screens using the YJ and LUCH reporter lines.
claims.source: Two mutants with reduced luciferase luminescence, one in each reporter background, were identified (Figure 1A) and RT-qPCR analysis confirmed reduced LUC expression in these mutant backgrounds relative to their respective controls (Figure 1B).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from genetic screens with data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: The same gene (At1g20870) was disrupted in both lil-1 and lil-2 mutants.
claims.source: Map-based cloning and candidate gene sequencing revealed that the same gene (At1g20870) was disrupted in both mutants.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from map-based cloning and sequencing.

claims.claim: The lil-1 allele contains a G-to-A mutation that disrupts the single splice acceptor site of At1g20870.
claims.source: The lil-1 allele contains a G-to-A mutation, which disrupts the single splice acceptor site of At1g20870 (Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from sequencing with data shown in the referenced figure.

claims.claim: The lil-2 allele contains a C-to-T mutation that introduces a premature stop codon.
claims.source: Although lil-2 was isolated from a T-DNA mutagenesis screen, this allele does not contain a T-DNA insertion, but instead contains a C-to-T mutation that introduces a premature stop codon (Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from sequencing with data shown in the referenced figure.

claims.claim: LIL is predicted to encode a 51.9 kDa protein containing a carboxy-terminal Alpha Crystallin Domain (ACD) or Heat Shock Protein 20 like (HSP20-like) chaperone domain.
claims.source: LIL is predicted to encode a 51.9 kDa protein containing a carboxy-terminal Alpha Crystallin Domain (ACD) or Heat Shock Protein 20 like (HSP20-like) chaperone domain (Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a prediction from protein sequence analysis with data shown in the referenced figure.

claims.claim: LIL and three paralogs form one clade among the 25 Arabidopsis ACD-containing proteins.
claims.source: Among the 25 Arabidopsis ACD-containing proteins, LIL and three paralogs form one clade (Scharf et al., 2001) (alignments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from phylogenetic analysis with data shown in the referenced figure and citation to prior work.

claims.claim: LIL (also known as INCREASED DNA METHYLATION 3 (IDM3) or INCREASED DNA METHYLATION 2-LIKE 1 (IDL1)) and ROS5/IDM2 were found to prevent DNA hyper-methylation and enable gene expression at other reporter transgenes and select genomic loci.
claims.source: Two members of this clade, LIL (also known as INCREASED DNA METHYLATION 3 (IDM3) [Lang et al., 2015] or INCREASED DNA METHYLATION 2-LIKE 1 (IDL1) [Li et al., 2015b]) and ROS5 (Zhao et al., 2014)/IDM2 (Qian et al., 2014) (At1g54840) were recently found to prevent DNA hyper-methylation and enable gene expression at other reporter transgenes and select genomic loci, demonstrating they also act to suppress gene silencing (Lang et al., 2015; Li et al., 2015b; Zhao et al., 2014; Qian et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to prior studies.

claims.claim: LIL interacts with three MBD proteins: MBD5, MBD6 and MBD7 in yeast two-hybrid assays.
claims.source: Using full-length LIL as bait and an Arabidopsis cDNA library as prey, LIL was found to interact with three MBD proteins: MBD5, MBD6 and MBD7 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from yeast two-hybrid experiments with data shown in the referenced figure.

claims.claim: An interaction was detected between the last MBD domain of MBD7 (MBD7d3) and the full length LIL protein.
claims.source: However, an interaction was detected between the last MBD domain of MBD7 (MBD7d3) and the full length LIL protein (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from yeast two-hybrid experiments with data shown in the referenced figure.

claims.claim: A 3x-Flag-tagged version of MBD5 co-purifies with ACD15.5 and ACD21.4 as well as low amounts of MBD6.
claims.source: Specifically, a 3x-Flag-tagged version of MBD5 (pMBD5::MBD5-3x-Flag) was shown to co-purify with ACD15.5 (At1g76440) and ACD21.4 (At1g54850) as well as low amounts of MBD6 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D)
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from affinity purification and mass spectrometry with data shown in the referenced figure.

claims.claim: Purification of a 3x-HA tagged version of MBD7 revealed a specific interaction with LIL.
claims.source: while purification of a 3x-HA tagged version of MBD7 (pMBD7::MBD7-3xHA) revealed a specific interaction with LIL (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from affinity purification and mass spectrometry with data shown in the referenced figure.

claims.claim: Purification of a 3x-Flag-tagged version of MBD7 yielded peptides corresponding to LIL, ROS4, ROS5, HDP1, and HDP2.
claims.source: As MBD7 had previously been shown to also associate with ROS4, ROS5 (Lang et al., 2015; Li et al., 2015b; Wang et al., 2015), and HARBINGER TRANSPOSON-DERIVED PROTEIN 1 (HDP1) and HDP2 (Duan et al., 2017), additional purifications using a 3x-Flag-tagged version of MBD7 (pMBD7::MBD7-3xFlag) were conducted and these experiments yielded peptides corresponding to LIL as well as all the aforementioned MBD7-associated proteins (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from affinity purification and mass spectrometry with data shown in the referenced figure and citations to prior work.

claims.claim: MBD5 and MBD7 associate with different subsets of ACD proteins to form distinct MBD-ACD protein complexes.
claims.source: Taken together, these findings demonstrate that MBD5 and MBD7 associate with different subsets of ACD proteins to form distinct MBD-ACD protein complexes, the roles and compositions of which are just beginning to be explored.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the affinity purification and mass spectrometry experiments.

claims.claim: The mbd5 mutations had no effect on LUC expression at the YJ reporter.
claims.source: The mbd5 mutations had no effect on LUC expression at the YJ reporter (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A,B).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from expression analysis with data shown in the referenced figure.

claims.claim: In the mbd7, ros4, and ros5 mutants, LUC expression was reduced to similar levels as observed in lil-1.
claims.source: Conversely, in the mbd7, ros4, and ros5 mutants, LUC expression was reduced to similar levels as observed in lil-1 (Figure 2A,B).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from expression analysis with data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: Expression of the d35S-driven NPTII gene present in both YJ and LUCH reporters was reduced in mbd7, ros4, ros5, and lil mutants.
claims.source: In addition, expression of the d35S-driven NPTII gene present in both YJ and LUCH reporters was also reduced in these mutants (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from expression analysis with data shown in the referenced figure.

claims.claim: Treatment with 5-Aza-dC results in increased LUC expression in both YJ and LUCH reporters.
claims.source: Previous analyses have shown that both the YJ (Li et al., 2016) and LUCH (Won et al., 2012) reporters are regulated by DNA methylation such that treatment with the cytosine methylation inhibitor 5-aza-2'-deoxycytidine (5-Aza-dC) results in increased LUC expression.
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to prior studies.

claims.claim: The levels of LUC expression in lil and mbd7 mutants treated with 5-Aza-dC were indistinguishable from their respective controls.
claims.source: To determine if DNA methylation is necessary for the phenotypes observed upon disruption of the MBD7 complex, we assessed the effects of 5-Aza-dC treatment on LUC expression in several alleles of lil and mbd7 and found the levels of LUC expression in these mutants were indistinguishable from their respective controls (Figure 3A,B).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from 5-Aza-dC treatment experiments with data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: LIL and MBD7 are only necessary for the expression of the LUC reporters when they harbor DNA methylation.
claims.source: Thus, LIL and MBD7 are only necessary for the expression of the LUC reporters when they harbor DNA methylation, affirming their roles in the transcriptional, rather than post-transcriptional, regulation of LUC expression.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the 5-Aza-dC treatment experiments.

claims.claim: Amplification of the d35S promoter was reduced in both lil mutants relative to their respective controls in McrBC restriction enzyme assays, indicating increased DNA methylation.
claims.source: Using this assay, amplification of the d35S promoter was reduced in both lil mutants relative to their respective controls, indicating that mutations in LIL increased the level of DNA methylation at the d35S promoter (Figure 4A; gel based).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from McrBC restriction enzyme assays with data shown in the referenced figure.

claims.claim: Similar results were obtained for lil-1, mbd7, ros4, and ros5 mutants when qPCR was performed to quantify DNA levels from mock or McrBC treated samples.
claims.source: Similar results were obtained for lil-1, mbd7, ros4, and ros5 mutants when qPCR was performed to quantify DNA levels from mock or McrBC treated samples (Figure 4B; qPCR).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from McrBC-qPCR assays with data shown in the referenced figure.

claims.claim: Quantification of the average methylation levels across the d35S promoter revealed a modest but consistent increase in DNA methylation in the CG context in lil-2, mbd7-5, and three biological replicates of lil-1.
claims.source: At the LUC reporters, quantification of the average methylation levels across the d35S promoter (282–1036 nt) revealed a surprisingly modest but consistent increase in DNA methylation in the CG context in lil-2, mbd7-5, and three biological replicates of lil-1 (Figure 4D).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from MethylC-seq analysis with data shown in the referenced figure.

claims.claim: The hyper-methylation in lil and mbd7 mutants is largely restricted to a small region at the 3' end of the d35S promoter.
claims.source: Further inspection of the DNA methylation profiles revealed that this hyper-methylation is largely restricted to a small region at the 3' end of the d35S promoter, which is within the region amplified in the McrBC-PCR methyl-cutting assays (Figure 4C; right panels).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from MethylC-seq analysis with data shown in the referenced figure.

claims.claim: In the lil-2 mutant, a slight increase in CG and CHG methylation, but no change in CHH methylation, was observed at the LUCH reporter.
claims.source: In the lil-2 mutant, a slight increase in CG and CHG methylation, but no change in CHH methylation, was observed at the LUCH reporter (Figure 4D; Full McrBC).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from MethylC-seq analysis with data shown in the referenced figure.

claims.claim: For the lil-1 replicates and mbd7-5, a more prominent increase in CG and CHG methylation was observed.
claims.source: For the lil-1 replicates and mbd7-5, a more prominent increase in CG and CHG methylation was observed, and these DNA methylation defects were significantly reversed by introduction of an MBD7-3xHA construct that rescues the LUC expression phenotype at the YJ reporter (Figure 4D short McrBC and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, respectively).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from MethylC-seq analysis with data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: Enrichment was observed at the d35S promoter using a MBD7-GFP line driven by a 35S promoter in ChIP experiments.
claims.source: While no enrichment was observed with either the 3xHA or 3xFlag tagged MBD7 proteins expressed under their native promoters, enrichment was observed at the d35S promoter using a previously characterized MBD7-GFP line driven by a 35S promoter (Wang et al., 2015) (Figure 4E).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from ChIP experiments with data shown in the referenced figure and citation to prior work.

claims.claim: The DNA methylation levels observed at the 35S promoter by traditional bisulfite sequencing show similar patterns of methylation in the lil and mbd7 mutants when compared to the MethylC-seq data.
claims.source: The DNA methylation levels observed at the 35S promoter by traditional bisulfite sequencing are represented in browser track format (Figure 5A and Supplementary file 1D: YJ_tradBS_WigTracks) and show similar patterns of methylation in the lil and mbd7 mutants when compared to the MethylC-seq data (Figure 4C,D), in that hyper-methylation (primarily in the CG and CHG contexts) was detected at the 3' end of the promoter (Figure 5A,B).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from traditional bisulfite sequencing with data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: The increased methylation observed in the mbd7-5 mutant was restored to a more wild-type level upon introduction of the pMBD7::MBD7-3xHA transgene.
claims.source: Also consistent with the MethylC-seq data, the increased methylation observed in the mbd7-5 mutant was restored to a more wild-type level upon introduction of the pMBD7::MBD7-3xHA transgene (Figure 5A,B).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from traditional bisulfite sequencing with data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: The traditional bisulfite sequencing revealed a uniform distribution of methylation at the YJ reporter.
claims.source: These analyses revealed a uniform distribution of methylation at the YJ reporter (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from traditional bisulfite sequencing with data shown in the referenced figure.

claims.claim: Decreases in non-CG methylation were observed in the ago4-6 and nrpe1-11 mutants predominantly at regions of the promoter producing large amounts of 24-nt siRNAs.
claims.source: At the level of DNA methylation, decreases in non-CG methylation were observed in the ago4-6 and nrpe1-11 mutants predominantly at regions of the promoter producing large amounts of 24-nt siRNAs, as predicted for components of the RNA-directed DNA methylation pathway (Figure 5A; '24-nt siRNA clusters').
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from traditional bisulfite sequencing with data shown in the referenced figure.

claims.claim: All three mutants (ago4-6, nrpe1-11 and rdd) showed a hyper-methylation phenotype similar to that observed in the lil and mbd7 mutants at the 3' end of the 35S promoter.
claims.source: Conversely, all three mutants (ago4-6, nrpe1-11 and rdd) showed a hyper-methylation phenotype similar to that observed in the lil and mbd7 mutants at the 3' end of the 35S promoter (Figure 5A,B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from traditional bisulfite sequencing with data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: Although the ago4-6, nrpe1-11 and rdd mutants exhibit similar hyper-methylation phenotypes in the CG and CHG contexts at the 3' end of the 35S promoter, LUC expression is much higher in the ago4 and nrpe1 mutants than in the rdd mutant.
claims.source: Notably, although the ago4-6, nrpe1-11 and rdd mutants exhibit similar hyper-methylation phenotypes in the CG and CHG contexts at the 3' end of the 35S promoter, LUC expression is much higher in the ago4 and nrpe1 mutants than in the rdd mutant (Figure 5C,D).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from expression and methylation analysis with data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: The hyper-methylation at the 3' end of the d35S promoter region alone is not sufficient to cause gene silencing at the YJ reporter.
claims.source: While compensatory effects on gene expression due to decreased non-CG methylation at other regions of the d35S promoter in the ago4 and nrpe1 mutants cannot be fully excluded, these findings suggest that the hyper-methylation at the 3' end of the d35S promoter region alone is not sufficient to cause gene silencing.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the analysis of ago4, nrpe1, and rdd mutants.

claims.claim: At the YJ reporter, the MBD7 complex can regulate gene expression in a manner that is largely downstream of DNA methylation.
claims.source: Taken together, these analyses reveal that at the YJ reporter the MBD7 complex can regulate gene expression in a manner that is largely downstream of DNA methylation.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the genetic uncoupling experiments.

claims.claim: Thousands of DMRs were identified in each of the lil-1 and mbd7 datasets, mostly in the CG and CHH contexts.
claims.source: Although thousands of DMRs were identified in each of the lil-1 and mbd7 datasets, mostly in the CG and CHH contexts (Supplementary file 2A), the vast majority of these DMRs were not in common between the different alleles or even between biological replicates (Supplementary file 2B-F, see orange highlighted comparisons).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from genome-wide MethylC-seq analysis.

claims.claim: When the DMRs from the three lil-1 replicates were compared with the DMRs identified in lil-2, mbd7-3 and mbd7-4, only 33 hyper and one hypo DMRs remained.
claims.source: Indeed, when the DMRs from the three lil-1 replicates were compared with the DMRs identified in lil-2, mbd7-3 and mbd7-4, only 33 hyper and one hypo DMRs remained (Figure 6A, Supplementary file 2F; 6-way DMR overlaps, and Supplementary file 2G-J), and these regions converged on 20 loci (19 displayed hyper-methylation and one showed hypo-methylation [Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1]).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from genome-wide MethylC-seq analysis with data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: Very few genomic targets show consistent changes in DNA methylation upon disruption of the MBD7 complex.
claims.source: Thus, while numerous DMRs can be identified between any single mbd7 or lil mutant vs. control (Supplementary file 2A), very few genomic targets show consistent changes in DNA methylation upon disruption of the MBD7 complex, indicating that these changes may represent natural variation in methylation.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from genome-wide MethylC-seq analysis.

claims.claim: A relaxed set of DMRs yielded 194 CG hyper DMRs, 310 CHG hyper DMRs and 52 CHH hyper DMRs.
claims.source: This yielded a set of 194 CG hyper DMRs, 310 CHG hyper DMRs and 52 CHH hyper DMRs (Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from relaxed DMR analysis with data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: Only a third of the hyper mC DMRs in mbd7 and lil mutants overlap with regions hyper-methylated in the rdd mutant background.
claims.source: Notably, only a third of these regions overlap with regions hyper-methylated in the rdd mutant background, representing a tiny fraction of the total rdd targets (Figure 6D).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from comparison of DMRs with data shown in the referenced figure.

claims.claim: The demethylation pathway does not appear to function in a manner that depends solely on either MBD7 or LIL.
claims.source: Thus, although there are clear genetic connections between MBD7, LIL and ROS1 in the regulation of several transgenic reporters (Lang et al., 2015; Li et al., 2015b; Wang et al., 2015), as a general rule, the demethylation pathway does not appear to function in a manner that depends solely on either MBD7 or LIL.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the DMR overlap analysis with citations to prior work.

claims.claim: Re-introduction of LIL is not able to efficiently correct the observed hyper-methylation defects.
claims.source: These findings demonstrate that re-introduction of LIL is not able to efficiently correct the observed hyper-methylation defects, which further supports the notion that these changes represent variation in methylation rather than a direct effect of the lil mutation.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from complementation experiments.

claims.claim: No overlapping mis-regulated genes were identified between the lil and mbd7 alleles in transcriptome profiling.
claims.source: Among these mutants, no overlapping mis-regulated genes were identified between the lil and mbd7 alleles (Supplementary file 3)
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from transcriptome profiling.

claims.claim: Only one of the genes previously identified as a target of MBD7 complex was consistently down-regulated in any of the mutants tested.
claims.source: and only one of the genes previously identified as a target of MBD7 complex (i.e. down-regulated genes associated with hyper DMRs in the Columbia ecotype (Lang et al., 2015; Li et al., 2015b; Qian et al., 2014; Duan et al., 2017; Qian et al., 2012)) was consistently down-regulated in any of the mutants tested (Figure 6—figure supplement 4).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a result from transcriptome profiling with data shown in the referenced figure and citations to prior work.

claims.claim: The MBD7 complex likely functions redundantly with other MBD-ACD complexes and/or is required only under specific conditions.
claims.source: Given the absence of detectable endogenous targets transcriptionally regulated by the MBD7 complex, it is likely that this complex functions redundantly with other MBD-ACD complexes and/or is required only under specific conditions.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a speculation based on the absence of endogenous targets.

claims.claim: Loss of the MBD7-LIL complex results in the silencing of LUC reporter constructs with minimal changes in DNA methylation.
claims.source: Nonetheless, our findings demonstrate that this complex has the ability to regulate gene expression in a manner largely downstream of DNA methylation at LUC reporters. Firstly, we found that loss of the MBD7-LIL complex results in the silencing of these reporter constructs with minimal changes in DNA methylation.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a summary of the study's findings.

claims.claim: Hyper-methylation at the 3' end of the d35S promoter in the YJ reporter does not appear to be sufficient to cause gene silencing.
claims.source: Secondly, we demonstrated that hyper-methylation at the 3' end of the d35S promoter in the YJ reporter does not appear to be sufficient to cause gene silencing (Figure 5).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a summary of the study's findings with reference to data shown in the figure.

claims.claim: MBD7 and LIL represent the first anti-silencing complex placed downstream of DNA methylation.
claims.source: However, unlike these other downstream effectors, which function to reinforce gene silencing, MBD7 and LIL represent the first anti-silencing complex placed downstream of DNA methylation, functioning to enable gene expression despite high levels of promoter DNA methylation.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a conclusion comparing the MBD7 complex to other known downstream effectors.

claims.claim: The MBD7 complex may function in a manner largely downstream of DNA methylation rather than as part of the DNA demethylation pathway.
claims.source: Rather than functioning as part of the DNA demethylation pathway, as has been previously hypothesized (Lang et al., 2015; Li et al., 2015b; Wang et al., 2015), our results suggest that the MBD7 complex may function in a manner largely downstream of DNA methylation.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the study's findings with citations to prior hypotheses.

claims.claim: The two ACD domain-containing proteins (LIL/IDL1/IDM3 and ROS5/IDM2) interact directly with each other.
claims.source: For example, the two ACD domain-containing proteins (LIL/IDL1/IDM3, and ROS5/IDM2) interact directly with each other (Li et al., 2015b), with MBD7 (Lang et al., 2015; Li et al., 2015b; Wang et al., 2015) and with ROS4/IDM1(Li et al., 2015b; Zhao et al., 2014; Qian et al., 2014), whereas MBD7 and ROS4/IDM1 fail to show a direct interaction (Lang et al., 2015; Li et al., 2015b).
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to prior studies.

claims.claim: MBD7 and ROS4/IDM1 fail to show a direct interaction.
claims.source: For example, the two ACD domain-containing proteins (LIL/IDL1/IDM3, and ROS5/IDM2) interact directly with each other (Li et al., 2015b), with MBD7 (Lang et al., 2015; Li et al., 2015b; Wang et al., 2015) and with ROS4/IDM1(Li et al., 2015b; Zhao et al., 2014; Qian et al., 2014), whereas MBD7 and ROS4/IDM1 fail to show a direct interaction (Lang et al., 2015; Li et al., 2015b).
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to prior studies.

claims.claim: The ACD-domain proteins may function to bridge the association between MBD7 and ROS4/IDM1.
claims.source: This suggests the ACD-domain proteins may function to bridge the association between MBD7 and ROS4/IDM1.
claims.evidence: This is stated as an inference from the interaction data.

claims.claim: ROS5/IDM2 forms higher-order structures that migrate at ~670 kDa after gel filtration, consistent with a 16-mer complex.
claims.source: Beyond these pair-wise interactions, Zhao et al. (2014) demonstrated that ROS5/IDM2 forms higher-order structures that migrate at ~670 kDa after gel filtration, consistent with a 16-mer complex.
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation to a prior study.

claims.claim: Loss of MORC1, MORC6, ATXR5 and ATXR6 results in de-compaction of peri-centromeric heterochromatin and the selective up-regulation of genes and transposons located within these regions.
claims.source: Many of these factors, including MORC1, MORC6, ATXR5 and ATXR6, influence chromatin organization on a gross scale, such that loss of these factors results in de-compaction of peri-centromeric heterochromatin (i.e., chromocenters) (Moissiard et al., 2012; Jacob et al., 2009) and the selective up-regulation of genes and transposons located within these regions (Moissiard et al., 2012; Jacob et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to prior studies.

claims.claim: MOM1 appears to act on a finer scale to influence gene expression without significantly perturbing chromatin compaction.
claims.source: On the other hand, MOM1 appears to act on a finer scale to influence gene expression without significantly perturbing chromatin compaction (Mittelsten Scheid et al., 2002; Probst et al., 2003).

results.result: Two independent genetic screens using YJ and LUCH reporter lines identified mutations in the same gene (At1g20870/LIL), which encodes a 51.9 kDa protein containing an Alpha Crystallin Domain (ACD). The lil-1 allele contains a G-to-A mutation disrupting the splice acceptor site, while lil-2 contains a C-to-T mutation introducing a premature stop codon.
results.evaluation: Claims C26-C31 provide converging evidence from independent genetic screens, molecular characterization, and sequence analysis. The identification of mutations in the same gene from two independent screens (C26-C27), combined with detailed molecular characterization of the mutations (C28-C29) and protein domain analysis (C30-C31), strongly supports this result.

results.result: LIL interacts with MBD proteins (MBD5, MBD6, MBD7) in yeast two-hybrid assays, and affinity purification experiments demonstrate that MBD5 and MBD7 associate with distinct subsets of ACD proteins to form separate MBD-ACD protein complexes. MBD7 specifically co-purifies with LIL, ROS4, ROS5, HDP1, and HDP2.
results.evaluation: Claims C33-C38 present complementary evidence from yeast two-hybrid assays (C33-C34) and mass spectrometry following affinity purification (C35-C37). The data consistently show protein-protein interactions and support the conclusion that distinct MBD-ACD complexes exist (C38). Multiple independent approaches converge on the same conclusion.

results.result: Mutations in mbd7, ros4, ros5, and lil result in reduced LUC and NPTII expression at the YJ and LUCH reporters, while mbd5 mutations have no effect on LUC expression.
results.evaluation: Claims C39-C41 are supported by RT-qPCR data and luciferase imaging shown in referenced figures. The consistent reduction in expression across multiple components of the MBD7 complex (C40-C41) contrasts with the lack of effect from mbd5 mutations (C39), providing clear functional distinction between the complexes.

results.result: Treatment with 5-Aza-dC eliminates the difference in LUC expression between lil/mbd7 mutants and controls, demonstrating that LIL and MBD7 are only necessary for LUC expression when DNA methylation is present.
results.evaluation: Claims C43-C44 are supported by 5-Aza-dC treatment experiments shown in Figure 3. The genetic uncoupling of the mutant phenotype by removal of DNA methylation provides strong evidence that the MBD7 complex functions in the context of methylated DNA, supporting a transcriptional rather than post-transcriptional role.

results.result: Mutations in lil and mbd7 result in modest increases in DNA methylation at the d35S promoter, primarily in the CG and CHG contexts, with hyper-methylation largely restricted to a small region at the 3' end of the promoter.
results.evaluation: Claims C45-C50 are supported by multiple complementary approaches: McrBC restriction enzyme assays (C45-C46) and high-resolution MethylC-seq analysis (C47-C50). The consistency across methods and biological replicates, combined with complementation experiments showing reversal of the phenotype (C50), provides strong support for this result.

results.result: Genetic uncoupling experiments demonstrate that hyper-methylation at the 3' end of the d35S promoter is not sufficient to cause gene silencing. The ago4, nrpe1, and rdd mutants all show similar hyper-methylation patterns, but LUC expression is much higher in ago4 and nrpe1 mutants than in rdd mutants.
results.evaluation: Claims C55-C59 present a critical genetic dissection showing that DNA methylation changes and gene expression phenotypes can be uncoupled. The comparison of ago4/nrpe1 mutants (which maintain high LUC expression despite hyper-methylation) with rdd mutants (which show silencing) provides strong evidence that the MBD7 complex functions largely downstream of DNA methylation (C59).

results.result: Genome-wide MethylC-seq analysis reveals minimal consistent changes in DNA methylation upon disruption of the MBD7 complex. Only 33 hyper and 1 hypo DMRs are shared across all lil and mbd7 datasets, and only about one-third of the relaxed set of DMRs overlap with regions hyper-methylated in rdd mutants.
results.evaluation: Claims C60-C65 are supported by comprehensive genome-wide MethylC-seq analysis across multiple alleles and biological replicates. The stringent overlap analysis (C61) and relaxed DMR analysis (C63-C64) both converge on the conclusion that very few genomic targets show consistent methylation changes (C62), and these represent only a small fraction of rdd targets (C64-C65). This strongly supports a role downstream of DNA methylation.

results.result: Re-introduction of functional LIL protein does not efficiently correct the observed hyper-methylation defects in lil mutants.
results.evaluation: Claim C66 is supported by complementation experiments using pLIL::9xMyc-LIL transgenic lines analyzed by MethylC-seq. The failure to rescue methylation defects at most DMRs, despite rescuing the LUC expression phenotype (shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3), further supports the interpretation that methylation changes represent natural variation rather than direct effects of the lil mutation.

results.result: Transcriptome profiling reveals no overlapping mis-regulated genes between lil and mbd7 alleles, and only one previously identified target gene shows consistent down-regulation in the mutants tested.
results.evaluation: Claims C67-C68 are supported by RNA-seq data across multiple alleles. The absence of consistent transcriptional changes at endogenous loci, despite clear effects at the transgenic reporters, suggests either redundancy with other complexes or condition-specific requirements for MBD7 complex function. The data quality and analysis appear sound.

results.result: The MBD7 complex suppresses transcriptional silencing of LUC reporters via a mechanism that is largely downstream of DNA methylation. The hyper-methylation and gene expression phenotypes can be genetically uncoupled, and genome-wide profiling shows minimal methylation changes, positioning the MBD7 complex as the first anti-silencing complex acting downstream of DNA methylation.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C5 and C70-C73 represent the major conclusions of the study, which are well-supported by the collective evidence from genetic uncoupling experiments (C3, C58-C59), genome-wide profiling (C4, C60-C65), and functional characterization (C43-C44, C70-C71). The convergence of multiple independent lines of evidence strongly supports the conclusion that the MBD7 complex functions primarily downstream of DNA methylation (C73) and represents a unique anti-silencing mechanism (C5, C72).

results.result: The YJ and LUCH reporters differ in basal LUC expression despite harboring nearly identical transgenes. Both have similar patterns of 24-nt siRNAs and DNA methylation at d35S promoters, but LUCH shows extended methylation into coding regions. Analysis suggests YJ represents a single-copy insertion while LUCH is a multi-copy insertion.
results.evaluation: Claims C21-C25 are supported by MethylC-seq and small RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1 and supplementary figures. The characterization of reporter differences provides important context for interpreting the genetic and molecular analyses. The inference about copy number (C24) is supported by analysis of chimeric reads in MethylC-seq data.

results.result: ChIP experiments using a MBD7-GFP line driven by a 35S promoter show enrichment at the d35S promoter of the YJ reporter, while native promoter-driven tagged versions show no enrichment.
results.evaluation: Claim C51 is supported by ChIP-qPCR data (Figure 4E), but the requirement for overexpression to detect binding raises questions about the physiological relevance of the interaction. The failure to detect enrichment with natively expressed tagged proteins could reflect technical limitations (low abundance, transient interactions) or suggest that overexpression creates non-physiological binding. Additional experiments would be needed to resolve this uncertainty.

results.result: Traditional bisulfite sequencing confirms the MethylC-seq results, showing similar hyper-methylation patterns in lil and mbd7 mutants at the 3' end of the 35S promoter, with rescue by MBD7-3xHA transgene. The methylation distribution is uniform rather than bimodal.
results.evaluation: Claims C52-C54 are supported by traditional bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1. The validation of MethylC-seq results using an independent method (C52) and the demonstration of uniform methylation distribution (C54) strengthen confidence in the methylation analysis. The complementation result (C53) is consistent with earlier data.

results.result: Analysis of MethylC-seq data indicates that the YJ reporter was inserted as a single copy into the At1g02740 3'UTR, while the LUCH reporter represents a multi-copy insertion with a complex structure including the entire binary vector.
results.evaluation: Claims C82-C83 are supported by detailed analysis of chimeric reads and coverage patterns in MethylC-seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2. The characterization of insertion sites and structures provides important context for understanding the different methylation patterns and expression levels of the two reporters.

results.result: The interaction between MBD7 and LIL can be mediated by multiple regions of MBD7, including both the StkC domain (previously identified) and the last MBD domain (identified in this study).
results.evaluation: Claims C84-C85 are supported by yeast two-hybrid data (Figure 2—figure supplement 1) combined with prior work (C84). The identification of an additional interaction domain (C85) extends previous findings and suggests multiple potential binding modes between MBD7 and LIL, which may have functional significance for complex assembly.

results.result: The MBD7 complex likely functions redundantly with other MBD-ACD complexes and/or is required only under specific conditions.
results.evaluation: Claim C69 is presented as speculation based on the absence of detectable endogenous targets (C67-C68). While this is a reasonable hypothesis given the existence of multiple MBD-ACD complexes (C38) and the clear function at transgenic reporters, it remains untested. The claim appropriately acknowledges uncertainty but requires future experimental validation.

results.result: In mbd7 and lil mutants, no obvious defects in chromocenter formation were observed, suggesting the MBD7 complex may act at a local level to enable expression of methylated genes, possibly antagonizing MOM1 function.
results.evaluation: Claim C80 is stated as an observation but no data is shown to support the assessment of chromocenter formation. Claim C81 is explicitly speculative, proposing a model for MBD7 function and potential antagonism with MOM1. While the speculation is reasonable given the known role of MOM1 at the LUCH reporter, it requires experimental validation.

results.result: The manuscript provides extensive background on DNA methylation pathways, MBD proteins, and factors acting downstream of DNA methylation in Arabidopsis, citing numerous prior studies.
results.evaluation: Claims C6-C20, C32, C42, and C74-C79 represent established knowledge from prior studies, appropriately cited throughout the manuscript. These claims provide essential context for interpreting the current findings but do not represent novel results from this study. The citations appear accurate and appropriate.
